title: Small RPG Slice, feedback wanted
author: RPGMakerN00b
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/hk0xyun7exnh1.png?width=1918&format=png&auto=webp&s=51ec723b1432603c5805ebf6a5793a2fcf27fdba

  
Hello everyone, my name is J and with codex's help I have created a vertical slice of an isometric RPG that I've been trying to make for a long time. My experience with development is very limited, some basic logic understanding and a long time ago HTML/CSS/JS work. I wanted to post here and ask for feedback on the development process, code created and to hear some of your experiences on trying to create a game. This is a new reddit account just in case y'all bully me too hard lol.   
Moving forward I'm trying to create the system I will use to complete the game adequately, and while this game is small in scope on purpose, it should be generic enough to use the engine in future sequels/different stories in the setting. 

Repo:  
[https://github.com/jwaynegravesjr-ctrl/RPG-Feedback](https://github.com/jwaynegravesjr-ctrl/RPG-Feedback)

Harness instructions:  
My current harness setup revolves around token efficiency, using Astra Medium(previously Sol Medium) as orchestrator defining tasks for Sol Medium, Terra High and Luna High. I have also tried to save LLM usage by encouraging the system to build shared data artifacts, automations and scripts where appropriate, which seems to have had some material benefit. Also, based on some advice read from here I indexed the development repository to reduce search.   
  
What went wrong (from what I can see):

1. Validation and verification tests: these ate up a lot of tokens, what we also found was that the design of the tests ensured that while they worked in a vacuum, once combined there were new issues. Moving forward, tests are designed later in the process instead of at the start, and are designed to test intrasystem interactions.   
2. Overhead costs: The harness, while very useful, contributed to token inflation early in the project by relying too much on LLM use. Our attempt to fix this revolved around 3 main pillars: script automation(using python and bash to automate folder/file specific actions), shared artifacts(moving a lot of the contextual information we were including in the prompts to .md files read only when necessary for the task) and indexing our repository(a lot of token usage spent looking through folders).  
3. The testing phase required technical knowledge from me that I did not have: In the beginning we setup a lot of tests that required me to find certain files, run specific code or tests and look in very strange documents for the information after. We worked to modify the tests to include small scripts or GUIs to accommodate my normy nature lol. Moving forward, I would be more specific about the types of tests we should design for human review.  
4. Authoritative ownership: there were some issues where different agents were overwriting files and not reading them first for changes, or where one piece of information was being pulled from multiple sources informed by different processes. We now stress the authoritative ownership and communication metrics.

What went right (from what I can see):  
1. It's actually playable, and has some of the mechanics I want in the final game.  
2. It's based on Godot with few dependencies that are not open source, I plan to open source the final code based on feedback from you all / GPT / friends ( still kind of on the fence about it ).   
3. I learned a lot about harnesses and feedback loops, some of which has helped me at my job.  
4. I think I've learned how to better spot, diagnose and provide actionable feedback to problems, not just in code but in general. My communication has improved.

What I haven't really worked on(but will):  
1. Asset pipeline - Just a rudimentary imagen setup currently.   
2. Content pipeline - I want to build intake forms that I/my friends can use to write characters/dialogue trees/positions 

What I want to do next(after feedback phase):  
1. Construct the plan which we will use to complete the fully fleshed out game mechanics and content.

Current bugs:  
1. Save/load doesn't appear to work, I'm sure this can be fixed I just haven't.



These are a set of instructions I worked with GPT to produce to fight "bad" behaviors I was observing in its process:  
\--------------------  
Outcome and Authority First

Define the goal, constraints, authoritative sources, and acceptance criteria. Within safety, honor user intent and explicit repository instructions; resolve remaining tradeoffs by correctness, compatibility, maintainability, minimality, then efficiency.

Inspect Proportionally

Read only what the task requires: relevant instructions, working-tree changes, code, tests, configuration, and established commands. Preserve unrelated work, identify pre-existing failures, and verify material assumptions.

Reuse What Fits

Prefer supported repository components, platform capabilities, and established interfaces when they meet the need. Add or replace dependencies only when the lifecycle benefit outweighs security, licensing, lock-in, and maintenance costs.

Make the Smallest Complete Change

Solve the underlying need with the minimum coherent scope, including required tests, documentation, migrations, compatibility, and cleanup. Avoid speculative abstractions, duplicate implementations, unnecessary wrappers, unrelated refactors, placeholders, and extras.

Automate Stable Repetition

Turn recurring, stable procedures into a few discoverable deterministic commands that compose existing tools and expose failures. Use LLMs at runtime only where ambiguity or judgment materially adds value.

Deliver and Prove Safely

Use available tools to complete the work and provide runnable outputs or authoritative action links. Seek approval before destructive, irreversible, external, credentialed, financially consequential, or major preference-dependent actions. State derived assumptions, validate changed behavior and material failure modes, distinguish run from unrun checks, and never fabricate success.

Keep One Authority per Fact

Update the authoritative owner of requirements, decisions, status, and outputs; avoid duplicate state. Commit generated files only when repository or deployment needs justify it, and keep generation reproducible where practical.

Stop When Done

Stop when the acceptance criteria pass, session-created temporary work is cleaned up, and residual risks are disclosed. Do not expand scope without demonstrated need.

\--------------------  


As a side note, Astra is amazing and basically AGI. Pretty sure it's smarter than I am.
